name: Airbus A330
summary: Long-range widebody twin sharing its wing with the A340; flown in the US by Delta (including the A330-900neo) and Hawaiian.

wings: Small, sharply canted angular winglets on the -200/-300
A330neo has long curved sharklet-style tips instead
engines: Two large underwing turbofans (CF6, PW4000 or Trent 700)
A330neo carries even bigger Trent 7000 nacelles
fuselage: Rounded Airbus nose with six-pane windshield
tail: Tall swept fin with a long dorsal fillet
Low-set tailplane; tailcone ends in a horizontal wedge

tellTales: Small sharp angled winglets on a long, slender twin-aisle twin
Long slim widebody with only two engines and a blunt rounded nose
Very long wingspan relative to the fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The A330 is longer and slimmer with a blunt Airbus nose and small angular winglets; the 767 is short and stubby with a pointed nose and, if fitted, tall blended winglets.
The A330 lacks the black 'raccoon mask' cockpit outline and has angular winglets (or straight sharklets) rather than the A350's swept-back curling tips.
The A330 has four-wheel main bogies and smaller engines; the 777 has six-wheel bogies, enormous round engines and a blade-like tailcone.
A civil A330 has no refuelling boom, drogue pods or military grey paint; the KC-46 is a 767 with a pointed nose and a boom under the tail.

usCount.source: Airline fleet data (Delta ~70 incl. A330-900neo, Hawaiian 24; planespotters.net)
